pages.text: "I'll jump in first!" Ppino the rabbit, always first at everything, pulled on a woolly hat. A big pile of leaves waited outside. Ppino slipped into orange shoes and pushed the door.
But the hat kept falling over their eyes. One ear was folded inside. "Ouch, my ear is squashed." Ppino pressed the hat down and ran out anyway.
The folded ear stung, and the hat kept slipping. Ppino stood holding it with both hands. The four had already plunged into the leaves, scattering them everywhere.
The leaf pile was flat now. Ppino hadn't even jumped in. Off came the hat, thrown to the ground. "I hate this hat!"
Grandma Bear sat on the doorstep and picked up the hat. "Ppino, this hat has two holes, right?" She turned it over to show the two ear holes.
"Two holes, two ears. Let them out one by one." Ppino took the hat and put one ear through a hole. The long ear slipped out.
Now the other one! Slowly, Ppino put the second ear through. Both stood up side by side. Mei the timid baby goat clapped. "Both ears out—all dressed!"
The hat no longer covered their eyes. Neither ear hurt. Ppino's long ears leaned forward first. "Now I'm really going!"
The leaves were piled high again. "One, hat on! Two, one ear out! Three, the other ear out!" With both ears standing tall, Ppino jumped in first.
Grandma gently stroked Ppino's two ears among the leaves. "The more you hurry, the more you need to count your ears first." Ppino shook off leaves and called, "Both ears out—all dressed!"
